requires: timeout_seconds is an int or float but not bool, is finite, and is greater than zero.
The probe runs before a live MCP test decides whether the host can create and operate subprocess stdio pipes.
The fixed probe child is independent of MathHead server startup and MCP protocol behavior.
ensures: The returned frozen StdioCapability has exactly one status from supported, unsupported, timed_out, or failed and a stable reason code.
supported is returned only after a fixed child process receives a sentinel on stdin, reproduces it on stdout, writes a distinct stderr sentinel, and exits zero.

unsupported is returned only for an allow-listed operating-system capability denial while creating or operating the fixed probe pipes; an MCP handshake, tool, schema, server-startup, or assertion defect is never classified unsupported.
timed_out is returned only when the fixed probe exceeds its explicit deadline and the child is reaped.
failed is returned for unexpected exceptions, nonzero exits, malformed probe output, or cleanup failure without hiding the stable failure category.
Live MCP tests skip only on unsupported; timed_out and failed remain test failures.
Every started child follows close, terminate, kill, wait, and stream-close cleanup as applicable, and no child is left running after return.
raises: Invalid timeout types or values raise TypeError or ValueError before a child process is started.
KeyboardInterrupt and SystemExit are not converted to capability results and cleanup still runs before propagation.
No expected capability denial, timeout, child failure, or cleanup failure leaks an unclassified traceback through the test selection boundary.

effects.process: starts at most one fixed current-interpreter probe child and always reaps it
effects.environment: reads the current interpreter and operating-system error information but does not mutate environment variables, locale, or global event-loop policy
effects.repository: never edits source, contracts, PLAN, TODO, PROGRESS, caches, or test artifacts

determinism.probe: the child program and sentinels are fixed constants and contain no clock, random, machine, checkout, or user data
determinism.classification: the same observable pipe outcome maps to the same status and reason code
determinism.diagnostics: reason codes exclude exception prose, absolute paths, process identifiers, and elapsed timings
determinism.skip: only the unsupported status is a capability skip; all other non-supported outcomes fail closed

budget.cancellation: cancellation closes stdin, terminates then kills if necessary, waits, closes remaining streams, and never returns supported

epistemics.supported: the independent fixed child completed the exact bidirectional stdio-pipe probe
epistemics.unsupported: an allow-listed host capability denial prevented the independent fixed pipe probe
epistemics.timed_out: the independent fixed pipe probe exceeded its deadline and was reaped
epistemics.failed: the probe result or cleanup was inconsistent, unexpected, or nonzero, so no capability claim is made
epistemics.application_test: once the independent probe is supported, every MCP startup, handshake, schema, tool-call, stdout-integrity, and shutdown defect remains a failing application test

invariants: A MathHead server or MCP protocol failure can never cause an unsupported result or skip.
A supported result requires exact stdin, stdout, stderr, and zero-exit evidence from the fixed child.
No result is returned while a probe child remains running or unreaped.
Unsupported reason codes come only from an explicit operating-system denial allow-list.
Timeout and cleanup defects fail closed and are never relabeled unsupported or supported.
Supported GitHub Windows, Linux, and macOS jobs execute live MCP assertions rather than skipping them.
